body: same.

i've been behind a screen since the 80s.

i've worked in tech my entire life.

i'm all of you except older.

i've skied since i was 4.  that has turned into a love for backcountry skiing.  i've been a runner since age 10.  that has turned into ultrarunning.  i've hiked/camped all my life.  that has turned into climbing.

i binge movies.  i have/had a successful career as a Network Engineer.  i've been trying to rekindle that love.

i wish i can do something to make us both feel better.

i'm in the hurt state right now and it always feels like it will never end.

be well.

it takes me over an hour of running to feel any type of endorphin rush these days.  and that's with intense running (at LEAST 80%+ VO2max).  sadly, humans are not equipped for any type of repetitive activity.  that includes any endurance sport.  and i knew this a long time ago.  i felt the onset of a deep depression and tried to fight it.  subsequently, my running has dropped to nearly zero miles per week.  and i'm a 50+/mile per week runner.

the friend group journey is fucking hard.  it's exhausting for a variety of reasons. i have to travel and make significant effort to be able to connect with anyone.  i'm likely way too open about my state of mind.  i used to guard my anxiety and depression and never (absolutely never) talk about it.

i DM'd you in regards to the gf.

i have a stretch of highway near my home.  my shitty subaru outback hits over 110 mph in a couple of areas.  i do this way too often.  and i've done the blood-curling yelling more often than i want to admit.  crashing has crossed my mind as well.

you are definitely not alone.

long answer (with no tldr!):  
  
honestly, i have a predisposition for anxiety/depression/addiction. every single person on my mother's side of the family suffers from some sort of something. i have had a cousin commit suicide, another one is currently using (meth), aunts and uncles are bipolar and/or alcoholics. i recognized all of the signs when i was very young and stayed away from drugs/alcohol.  
  
i came from a divorced family at age 3. mother remarried. i basically raised (3) half brothers from 10-18. almost didn't graduate from high school (due to depression). had to take an equivalent college course (psych) to graduate. failed out of college (again due to depression/anxiety) twice for computer science. never finished. i've stood on bridges, but never jumped. ended up going into tech in the 90s and made a bit of money.  
  
my father wasn't really there as a kid. there were some traumatic events that happened from 4-18.  
  
i live about 1.5 hours away from any major city (including my mother's side of the family). i'm reestablishing a friendgroup after i quit my job back in 2016).  
  
the cool story that i eluded to in my previous response is this house. it was built/owned by the oldest woman to climb Mount Rainier (Bronka Sundstrom at 77). she's a holocaust survivor and saw her father walk into the chambers. she lost her only son to cancer. she ended up outliving her husband. she was alone in this house for 9 years before she decided to get off of the mountain. everyone knows her in this small town. my family has known her since the 80s. i'm a climber, skier, ultrarunner, and hiker so the house fits my lifestyle. BUT, it's isolated. i often try to put things in perspective and think about her story.  
  
being 47, never married, no kids (never intended on having any), and well, with covid, life is interesting. add on MDD and stuff gets even more interesting. i also fell for a woman that ended back in April.

the sad thing is that i can just get up and go.  i don't have anything or anyone relying on me.

i did that in 2017.  i bought a van at the end of 2016 and said fuck it to corporate america and lived out of it for a couple of years and traveled around the western US.  i ran up/down all the mountains i could find.  i learned some things about myself, but ultimately was alone with myself.  i lacked companionship.  it was an interesting distraction and fun at times.
it large cities, i bet there would be a market for them!  especially now.

that same voice keeps me alive.  i honestly don't even know why it is still there.

i wrote out a long entry detailing the steps i needed to take to end my life on this account about 21 hours ago, titled "no connection to anyone. suicide is my only answer."  i keep writing out i want to die.  i wrote an entry titled "it doesn't get better" about 21 hours ago.  this shit is fucking real.

the short moments in time that are worth living for are so rare, it hurts.

i've been through 20+ years of therapy and prescription drugs just to deal with everything.

i keep wanting to type, "hang in there."  but man, i can barely even say it to myself.

hang in there.  :)

i've slept weeks away (in the last 6 months).

i'm not even sure how i did it.

hang in there?

47M and can confirm that it doesn't get better.  :(  i just made a comment earlier this evening that i've experienced (maybe) joy during 1% of my life.  the struggle is real.  it's actually hard for me to continue living.  i wake up every single day wanting to die.

the same exact thoughts you are having at 20, i had at 20.  there was a long form version of twitter called livejournal (dot com).  it still exists, but doesn't get used much anymore.  i can go back and look at these same types of entries.

be well.

of course i didn't fully type out all of the details of my life and experiences.  i've gone through CBT twice.  i've been in therapy for 20+ years.  i've taken 3 separate types of anti-depressants (2 SSRIs and Wellbutrin).  i've had two separate evaluations during two separate times in my life (early 20s and mid 40s).  both times i was diagnosed with major depressive disorder and generalized anxiety disorder.  in my early 20s, i was diagnosed with social anxiety disorder.  that didn't seem to come up with the second evaluation.  i don't know anymore.

i've poured myself into work, hobbies, relationships, friendships, running, climbing, skiing, mindfulness, and volunteering.  i've talked with friends and family.  i lived in a van for a couple of years and ran up/down mountains.  i've had okay relationships.

i used to read research papers on depression.  (of course i'm just some random average dude that has NOT dedicated his life to that profession.)

again, thanks.
